# AI-DECLARATION.md

> The most popular open standard for declaring how much AI was involved in building a software project. A project adds an `AI-DECLARATION.md` file to its repository stating an overall involvement level, and optionally a breakdown by process and by component.

The file is plain Markdown with YAML front matter. Levels run from no AI involvement through to fully AI-generated, and a declaration is a claim by the project author, not an audit or a certification by anyone else.

## Specification

- [Specification v0.1.2 (English)](https://ai-declaration.md/en/0.1.2/): the full standard in English
- [Specification v0.1.2 (한국어)](https://ai-declaration.md/ko/0.1.2/): the full standard in 한국어
- [Specification v0.1.2 (Português (Brasil))](https://ai-declaration.md/pt-br/0.1.2/): the full standard in Português (Brasil)
- [Specification v0.1.2 (中文)](https://ai-declaration.md/zh/0.1.2/): the full standard in 中文

## Tools

- [Validate](https://ai-declaration.md/validate/): paste a declaration and check it against the specification
- [Directory](https://ai-declaration.md/directory/): public GitHub repositories that publish a declaration
- [API](https://ai-declaration.md/api/): read-only JSON API to detect and validate declarations, no key required
- [ai-declaration Reddit bot](https://developers.reddit.com/apps/ai-declaration/): comments on Reddit posts with what a linked repository declares

## Resources

- [yujqiao/ai-declare](https://github.com/yujqiao/ai-declare): agent skill that generates an `AI-DECLARATION.md` for a project
- [DimwitLabs/ai-declare](https://github.com/DimwitLabs/ai-declare): fork of the above that reads the specification and validates through the [API](https://ai-declaration.md/api/)
